title: Protocol for subcellular targeted microthermal protein damage in cells cultivated on plasmonic nanosilver-modified surfaces
protocol: Prepare stock solutions of silver nitrate (0.005 M), ammonia solution (0.1 M), sodium citrate (1% w/w), sodium borohydride (0.001 M), and hydrazine monohydrate (0.05 M) with water.
Add 5 mL of silver nitrate, 1.25 mL of ammonia solution, 1.25 mL of sodium citrate, and 13.425 mL of distilled water into a 50 mL beaker while stirring continuously.
Add 0.075 mL of sodium borohydride and 4 mL of hydrazine to the mixture in the beaker.
Stir the solution for 5 minutes.
Measure UV-VIS absorption spectra of the solution.
Functionalize cell culture plates by filling up the wells with 1% polyacrylic acid (PAA).
After a 2-hour functionalization period, pour out PAA from the wells and wash them under running distilled water.
Coat each well surface by filling up the wells for 2 hours with 1% poly(diallyl dimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA).
Pour out unabsorbed PDDA from the wells and wash properly by running distilled water.
Fill up the wells with AgNPs dispersion and leave still for 45 minutes to deposit AgNPs on the well surface.
Empty the wells, wash them with distilled water, and air-dry.
Seed the desired cell line using standard cell culture protocol.
Use between 80,000 and 100,000 cells per well for optimal confluency in a 24-well plate.
Place the well plate with cells on a prewarmed (35°C-37°C) confocal microscope.
Wait approximately 15 minutes to allow temperature equilibration.
Visualize the cells expressing GFP using a blue laser and appropriate filters.
Set the focus of the objective to the plasmon layer by finding the interface between the cell body and the bottom of the well surface.
Alternatively, visualize the plasmon layer using transmission light mode.
Activate the plasmon layer with a 561 nm solid-state laser or another appropriate laser with similar wavelength.
Regulate emitted heat through laser power, pixel dwell time, and number of irradiation cycles.
Determine the appropriate setup experimentally due to differences between microscopes and lasers.
Visualize cells (GFP-reporter) by 488 nm laser.
